subject: Service degradation: intermittent 5xx/429 timeouts impacting Nimbus production
messages:

Date: Fri, 14 Feb 2026 08:58:12 -0800
Subject: URGENT: Increased 5xx/429s and client timeouts (production)

Stephanie —

We're seeing a sudden spike of 5xx and 429s from Redwood’s API hitting our production fleet since ~08:30 PST. A few notes:

- Error rate observed: ~6% 5xx and ~4% 429s across user-facing endpoints (historical baseline <0.5%).
- Impact: application calls timing out for end users, session-level retries visible in our logs, and a large number of automated retries amplified traffic.
- Affected region: us-west primarily, but some requests in us-east showing higher latency as well.

We’re mid-launch for a marketing campaign and this is customer-facing. Can you confirm you’ve seen this, provide ETA on mitigation, and open an incident? We need an immediate call with someone from infra and an exec point-of-contact.

I’ve attached a short sample of client-side logs and a screenshot of our dashboard.

—Kate

Date: Fri, 14 Feb 2026 09:38:47 -08:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Increased 5xx/429s and client timeouts (production)

Summary of immediate triage from bridge:

- Observed behavior: a cascade effect where timeouts at downstream embedding/kv-cache layer triggered client retries; retries are being accepted (no effective client-side rate limiting) and are amplifying load on our L2 inference pool. This causes transient OOMs and short-lived 5xx bursts, and our API layer returns 429s when queue depth exceeds threshold.
- Short-term mitigations applied (09:30 PST):
  * Enabled stricter connection queue limits on the gateway (reduced queue depth to limit tail latency amplification).
  * Deployed temporary backpressure filter that returns a 503 w/ Retry-After when downstream load passes threshold.
  * Increased worker pool for embeddings by 20% in us-west region (burst capacity).
- Evidence: attaching support-log-export and SLO dashboard snapshot.

Immediate asks from ops:
- Nimbus: if you can throttle aggressive client-side retries for 10–20 minutes while we stabilize, that will reduce amplification.
- Stephanie: escalate if additional exec pressure so we can prioritize capacity.

We’ll keep the bridge open and follow up with a short postmortem draft within 48 hours.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kate Miller <kate.miller@nimbusapps.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:02:13 -08:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & recommended follow-ups (draft)

Hi all —

Below is a concise post-incident summary and proposed action items (this is a draft for Stephanie/exec review before we publish to Nimbus and internal stakeholders). Feedback welcome.

Incident summary:
- Window: 2026-02-14 08:30–10:05 PST (primary impact), with residual elevated retries until 12:00 PST.
- Root cause (primary): competitive eviction and miss patterns in the L1 prefix cache caused higher-than-expected pressure on the L2 embedding service. The embedding service's autoscaler reacted slowly to the steep request burst due to conservative CPU thresholds; combined with lack of circuit-breaker on the embedding client, retry storms amplified load and produced transient OOMs -> 5xx.
- Monitoring gap: we did not have an alert tied to error budget burn rate or 99th percentile latency crossing a sustained threshold for more than 5m. The gateway alerting only monitored overall 5xx rate, not tail behavior or downstream saturation.

Customer impact: Nimbus saw user-facing timeouts and degraded UX during prime campaign hours. Estimated customer error budget consumption: ~35% of weekly SLO for the service.

Actions taken during incident:
- Short-term: applied stronger gateway queue limits, temporary backpressure replies (503 w/ Retry-After), 20% burst capacity add, and manual eviction tuning on the prefix cache.
- Stabilized services and closed the immediate incident at ~10:05 PST.

Recommended follow-ups (owner / ETA):
1) Alerting: Create an "SLO burn" alert and a 99p latency sustained (>5m) alert for gateway and embedding service. Owner: Jonas (infra/monitoring). ETA: 7 days.
2) Runbooks: Publish an embedding-service runbook with step-by-step mitigation (drain pool, apply backpressure, toggle cache thresholds). Owner: Rishi. ETA: 3 days.
3) Circuit-breakers + client-sdk soft-fail: Add client-side guidance and automatic circuit-breakers in the gateway when downstream error budget is low. Owner: Platform. ETA: 21 days.
4) Capacity policy: Revisit autoscaler thresholds for embedding workers and add a fast-burst path for load spikes. Owner: Infra. ETA: 14 days.
5) SLO tuning: Re-evaluate SLOs for tail latency and set tolerances for campaign-like traffic patterns; include a documented rollback policy. Owner: Product + SRE. ETA: 10 days.
6) Customer comms: Draft a customer-facing incident summary and compensation offer (credits) for Nimbus. Owner: Stephanie / CS. ETA: 48 hours.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-2026-02-16.md (attached), Grafana snapshots, support logs.

We should schedule an executive sync with Nimbus to go through the action plan and commit to delivery windows. Proposed slot: Tue 2026-02-17 09:00 PST (30 min).

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
